akhfash:153-153.t:
Allah the Exalted said ﴿إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ وَلاَ تَلْوُونَ عَلَىٰ أحَدٍ﴾, because you say "أَصْعَد", meaning: he went on and travelled, and "أَصْعَدَ الوُادي", meaning: he went down into it. As for "صَعِدَ", it means: he climbed (ارتفى).
And He said ﴿فَأَثَابَكُمْ غُمّاً بِغَمٍّ﴾, i.e. "upon (عَلى) grief". It is as He said ﴿فِي جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ﴾, whose meaning is "on (على) the trunks of the palm trees", and as one says "ضَرَبَني فِي السيفِ" meaning "بِالسيف" (with the sword), and you say "نزلت في أبيك", i.e. "على أَبيك" (I stayed with your father as a guest).

akhfash:154-154.t:
Allah the Exalted said ﴿إِنَّ ٱلأَمْرَ كُلُّهُ للَّهِ﴾ — [nominative] if you make "كُلاًّ" a noun [i.e. a mubtadaʾ (subject)], as in your saying "إنَّ الأَمْرَ بَعْضُهُ لِزَيْدٍ"; and if you make it a ṣifa (qualifier) you put it in the accusative. And if you wish you may put it in the accusative as a badal (substitute), because if you said "إنَّ الأَمْرَ بَعْضَهُ لِزَيْدٍ" it would be permissible as a badal, whereas the ṣifa does not occur with "بَعْض". The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is the one hundred and sixty-first shāhid (illustrative verse)]:
إنَّ السُّيُوفَ غُدُوُّها وَرَواحُها * تَركا فَزارَةَ مثلَ قَرْنِ الأَعْضَبِ
(Verily the swords — their going out at morning and their return at evening left [the tribe of] Fazāra like the horn of the broken-horned [animal].)
So he made "الغُدُوّ" and "الرواحَ" a mubtadaʾ and assigned the verb to them. Some put "غُدُوَّها" and "رَواحَها" in the accusative and said "تركتْ هَوازِنَ", thus assigning the "leaving" to "the swords" and making "the going out at morning" and "the return at evening" follow it like a ṣifa, so that it came to be in the position of "كلّهَا". And you say ﴿إِنَّ ٱلأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ للَّهِ﴾ as tawkīd (emphasis); this is better, and it is how we read it.
And Allah the Exalted said ﴿لَبَرَزَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَتْلُ إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمْ﴾. Some have said ﴿القِتالُ﴾, but "القَتْلُ" is [more correct] in our view; and some have said ﴿إلى قِتالِهِم﴾, but ﴿القَتْلُ﴾ is the more correct of the two, if Allah wills, because He said ﴿إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمْ﴾ (to their places of lying down).
And He said ﴿وَلِيَبْتَلِيَ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ﴾, i.e. "so that (كَيْ) Allah may test".

akhfash:156-156.t: Allah the Exalted said ﴿أَوْ كَانُواْ غُزًّى لَّوْ كَانُواْ عِنْدَنَا مَا مَاتُواْ وَمَا قُتِلُواْ﴾. The singular of "الغُزَّى" is "غاز" (raider), like "شاهِد" and "شُهَّد".

akhfash:157-157.t: Allah the Exalted said ﴿وَلَئِنْ قُتِلْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْ مُتُّمْ﴾ — the verse. If it is asked: how can ﴿لَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ be the answer to that first part? [The answer is that] it is as though, when He said ﴿وَلَئِنْ قُتِلْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْ مُتُّمْ﴾, forgiveness and mercy were called to their minds, since that was in the path [of Allah]; so He said ﴿لَمَغْفِرَةٌ﴾, meaning: "that forgiveness ﴿خَيْرٌ مِمّا تَجْمَعُونَ﴾ (is better than what they amass)".

akhfash:158-158.t: He said ﴿وَلَئِنْ مُّتُّمْ أَوْ قُتِلْتُمْ لإِلَى ٱلله تُحْشَرُونَ﴾, and if you wish you may say ﴿قُتِّلْتُمْ﴾.

akhfash:159-159.t: Allah the Exalted said ﴿فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, meaning: "فَبِرَحْمَةٍ" (so by a mercy), and ﴿ما﴾ is zāʾida (redundant).

akhfash:161-161.t: Allah the Exalted said ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ﴾, and some read ﴿يُغَلُّ﴾. Both are correct — and Allah knows best — because the meaning is "that he should betray" or "that he should be betrayed".

akhfash:165-165.t: He said ﴿أَوَ لَمَّا أَصَابَتْكُمْ مُّصِيبَةٌ﴾. This alif is the alif of interrogation, which has entered upon the wāw of conjunction (ʿaṭf). It is as though He said: "You did such-and-such, and when [disaster] struck you…", and then the alif of interrogation was put in front of the wāw.

akhfash:166-166.t:
Allah the Exalted said ﴿وَمَآ أَصَابَكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْتَقَى ٱلْجَمْعَانِ فَبِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾. He put the khabar (predicate) with fāʾ because ﴿ما﴾ is in the position of "الذي" (that which), and it has the meaning of "مَنْ"; and "مَنْ" occurs in conditional constructions (al-mujāzāh), with its answer taking fāʾ.
He said ﴿فَبِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: He put the khabar with fāʾ because ﴿مَآ أَصَابَكُمْ﴾ means "that which struck you". And He said ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ because its meaning is: "فَهُوَ بإِذن اللّهِ" (it is by Allah's permission) "وَهُوَ لِيَعْلَم" (and it is so that He may know).

akhfash:168-168.t: He said ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ لإِخْوَانِهِمْ وَقَعَدُواْ لَوْ أَطَاعُونَا مَا قُتِلُوا قُلْ فَادْرَءُوا عَنْ أَنْفُسِكُمُ الْمَوْتَ﴾, i.e. "Say to them: ﴿فَادْرَءُوا عَنْ أَنْفُسِكُمُ الْمَوْتَ﴾", and "لَهُمْ" (to them) is left implied.

akhfash:173-173.t: Allah the Exalted said ﴿فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَاناً﴾, meaning: "فَزادَهُمْ قَوْلُهُم إيمانا" (so their saying [that] increased them in faith).

akhfash:175-175.t: He said ﴿إِنَّمَا ذٰلِكُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ﴾, meaning: "يُرْهِبُ النَّاسَ أولِياءَهُ" (he frightens people with his allies), i.e. "بِأَوّلِيائِهِ" (by means of his allies).

akhfash:180-180.t: He said ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِمَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ هُوَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ بَلْ هُوَ شَرٌّ لَّهُمْ﴾. He meant "وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ البُخْلَ هُوَ خَيْراً لَهُمْ" (do not reckon the stinginess to be better for them), and dropped the noun upon which the reckoning falls, namely "البُخْل" (stinginess), because He had mentioned the reckoning and mentioned what Allah gave them of His bounty, so He left both implied since He had mentioned them. And there has come an ellipsis more severe than this: Allah the Exalted said ﴿لاَ يَسْتَوِي مِنكُم مَّنْ أَنفَقَ مِن قَبْلِ ٱلْفَتْحِ وَقَاتَلَ﴾ and He did not say "وَمَنْ أَنْفَقَ مِنْ بَعْد" (and the one who spent afterwards), because when He said ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنفَقُواْ مِن بَعْدُ﴾ there was in it an indication that He meant them.

akhfash:181-181.t: Allah the Exalted said ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَالُواْ وَقَتْلَهُمُ ٱلأَنبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ﴾, while a long age had passed since that [killing]; so He only means: We shall record what they said against whoever approved of it after them, in the days when he approves of it.

akhfash:187-187.t: He said ﴿لَيُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَهُ﴾, meaning: "He made them swear: they shall surely make it clear and shall not conceal it". And He said ﴿لَتُبيِّنَنَّهُ وَلا تَكْتُمونَهُ﴾, i.e. "Say to them: By Allah, you shall surely make it clear and shall not conceal it".

akhfash:188-188.t: As for His saying ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَوْاْ وَّيُحِبُّونَ أَن يُحْمَدُواْ بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُواْ فَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ﴾, the latter one is a badal (substitute) from the former, and the fāʾ is zāʾida (redundant). I do not like the reading of whoever reads the first one with yāʾ, [since] it has no valid way in Arabic, because if he says ﴿لاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَوْاْ﴾ he has not made it fall on anything [i.e. the verb has no objects].

akhfash:195-195.t: He said ﴿أَنِّي لاَ أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِّنْكُمْ مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَىٰ﴾, i.e. "so He answered: [saying] that I do not let the deed of any doer among you be lost". He put ﴿مِنْ﴾ in it as zāʾida (redundant), as you say "قَدْ كانَ مِنْ حَدِيثٍ" (there has been some talk), and ﴿مِنْ﴾ here is superfluous (laghw), because the particle of negation has entered in His saying ﴿لا أُضِيعُ﴾.

akhfash:2-2.t: As for His saying ﴿ٱلْحَيُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ﴾, ﴿ٱلْقَيُّومُ﴾ is [on the pattern] "الفَيْعُول", but when a quiescent yāʾ comes before a vowelled wāw, the wāw is turned into yāʾ; its origin is "القَيْوُومُ". (الدَّيَّانُ) is "الفَيْعَال", and "الدَّيَّارُ" is "الفَيْعال"; it is from "دَارَ", "يَدُورُ", and its origin is "الدَيْوارُ", but the wāw was turned into yāʾ.

akhfash:3-3.t: As for ﴿مُصَدِّقاً لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾, it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

akhfash:4-4.t: He said: ﴿هُدىً لِّلنَّاسِ﴾. ﴿هُدَىً﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), but ﴿هُدَىً﴾ ends in a short alif (maqṣūr), so it is left in one state.

akhfash:11-11.t: He said: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾. He is saying: "like their habit in evil", from "دَأَبَ", "يَدْأَبُ", "دَأَباً" (to persist in a habit).

akhfash:12-12.t: He said: ﴿قُلْ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَتُغْلَبُونَ وَتُحْشَرُونَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ﴾, that is: [say] "you will be overcome". Just as you say "Say to Zayd: 'You will go'", that is: [tell him] that you will go. Some read ﴿سَيُغْلَبُون﴾, that is: say to them what I say; and what I say [about] them is "they will be overcome". And He said ﴿قُل لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ إِن يَنتَهُواْ يُغَفَرْ لَهُمْ مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ وَإِنْ يَعُودُواْ﴾; this can only be with yāʾ [i.e. third person] in the Qur'an, because He said ﴿يُغَفَرْ لَهُمْ﴾; had it been with tāʾ [second person] He would have said ﴿يُغْفَرْ لَكُم﴾. In ordinary speech it is permissible with tāʾ, and you make it "لَكُمْ", as I have explained to you.

akhfash:13-13.t:
And He said: ﴿قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ ٱلْتَقَتَا فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَأُخْرَىٰ كَافِرَةٌ﴾: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), as though He had said "one of them is a party fighting in the way of Allah". It has also been read in the genitive, according to the first part of the statement, as a badal (substitute), and that is permissible. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-third shāhid (attested verse)]:
وَكُنْتُ كَذِي رِجْلَيْنِ رِجْلٌ صَحِيحَةٌ * وَرِجْلٌ بِها رَيْبٌ مِنَ الحَدَثان
(I was like a man with two legs: a sound leg, and a leg struck by one of fate's mishaps.)
He used the nominative. Some put it in the genitive as a badal, and some use the nominative on [the meaning] "one of them is such, and the other is such". And he said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-fourth shāhid]:
[و] إنَّ لها جارَيْنِ لَنْ يَغْدرا بها * ربيبُ النَبِيِّ وابنُ خَيْرِ الخَلائِفِ
([And] she has two protectors who will never betray her: the Prophet's stepson and the son of the best of caliphs.)
Nominative; and the accusative [would be] as a badal. And He the Exalted said ﴿هَـٰذَا [ذِكْرٌ] وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾ ﴿جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾: if you wish you may make "جنات" a badal as well; and if you wish you may put it in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ", or on [the meaning] "they are gardens", beginning with it. This cannot be on [the pattern] "one of them is such", because that meaning is not in it; and no one read it in the nominative. And He the Exalted said ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ﴾, accusative as a badal; the nominative may also occur in it, on [the meaning] "they are the jinn". And He the Exalted said ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نِبِيٍّ عَدُوّاً شَيَاطِينَ ٱلإِنْسِ﴾, as a badal, and nominative on [the meaning] "they are devils"; as though, when he uses the nominative, he were asked — or knew that he would be asked — "What are they?" or "Who are they?", and he said: "They are such-and-such". And when he uses the accusative, it is as though he were asked — or knew he would be asked — "He made what?" or "They made what?". Or it may be that the verb falls on "the devils", [and] ﴿عَدُوّاً﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Like it is ﴿لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ﴾ ﴿نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ﴾, as though that were asked or known, and he said "by a forelock"; the nominative may also occur in it, on [the question] "What is it?", so he says ﴿نَاصِيَةٍ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the nominative نَاصِيَةٌ is meant], and the accusative as a ḥāl. The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-fifth shāhid]:
إنّا وَجَدْنا بَنِي جُلاَّنَ كُلَّهُمُ * كَسَاعِدِ الضَّبِّ لا طُولٌ وَلا عِظَمُ
(We have found the Banū Jullān, all of them, like the foreleg of a lizard: no length and no bulk.)
As a badal, that is: like "no length and no bulk". And like the [nominative as] mubtadaʾ is ﴿قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ﴾.

akhfash:14-14.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ ٱلْمَآبِ﴾. The place of the first radical (fāʾ) in it has hamza, because it is from "آبَ", "يَؤوُبُ" (to return), and it has a weak middle radical (ʿayn), like "قُلْتَ", "تَقُولُ", whose "مَفْعَل" is "مَقال". You say "آبَ", "يَؤوبُ", "إياباً". Allah the Exalted said ﴿إِنَّ إِلَيْنَآ إِيَابَهُمْ﴾, and it is returning. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-sixth shāhid]:
فَأَلْقَتْ عَصاها وَاسْتَقَرَّ بِها النَّوى * كَما قَرَّ عَيْناً بالإِيابِ المُسافِرُ
(So she threw down her staff and her journey came to rest, as the traveller's eye is gladdened by the homecoming.)
As for "الأوّابُ", it is the one who returns to the truth, and it is from "آبَ", "يَؤوبُ" [too]. As for His saying ﴿يٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ﴾, it is as they mention: glorification; or it is — and Allah knows best — like the first: He is saying "return to the truth", and "الأوّابُ" is the one who returns to the truth.

akhfash:15-15.t: His saying ﴿قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ مِّن ذٰلِكُمْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَأَزْوَاجٌ مُّطَهَّرَةٌ﴾: it is as though it were said to them "What do they have?" and "What is that?", and it was said: "It is such-and-such". As for ﴿بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكَ مَثُوبَةً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, it is only on [the pattern] "I shall inform you of something worse than that in reckoning" and "of something better than that in reckoning". His saying ﴿مَن لَّعَنَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from His saying ﴿بِشَرٍّ﴾, and nominative on [the meaning] "it is the one whom Allah has cursed".

akhfash:17-17.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿ ٱلصَّابِرِينَ﴾ up to His saying ﴿بِٱلأَسْحَارِ﴾: in the position of the genitive, [following] ﴿لِلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا﴾; it is made genitive by this added lām.

akhfash:18-18.t: He said: ﴿شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لاَ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ وَٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلْعِلْمِ قَآئِمَاً بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾: it is only "they bore witness that there is no god but He, maintaining justice"; ﴿قَائِماً﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

akhfash:19-19.t: He said: ﴿إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ بَغْياَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾. He is saying: ﴿وَمَا ٱخْتَلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾ ﴿بَغْياَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ ﴿إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ﴾ [i.e. "those given the Book did not differ, out of envy among themselves, except after knowledge had come to them"].

akhfash:28-28.t:
And He said: ﴿لاَّ يَتَّخِذِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ with kasra on ﴿يَتَّخِذِ﴾, because a quiescent lām met it while it is a prohibition [i.e. jussive and quiescent], so he gave it kasra.
And He the Exalted said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَتَّقُواْ مِنْهُمْ تَقِيَّةً﴾. Some read ﴿تُقَاةً﴾. Each is [good] Arabic, and ﴿تُقَاةٌ﴾ is better, like "إِتَّكَأَ" – "تُكَأَةً" (to lean / a support), "إتَّخم" – "تُخَمَةً" (to suffer indigestion / indigestion) and "إتَّحَفَ" – "تُحْفَةً" (to present / a gift).

akhfash:30-30.t: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَدَاً بَعِيداً﴾, because "البَيْنَ" here is an adverbial (ẓarf) and not a noun; had it been a noun, "الأمَدُ" would have been nominative. When you bring something that is an adverbial for the other and make the accusative particles fall on it, use the accusative, as in your saying "إنَّ عِنْدَنا زَيْداً" ("Zayd is with us"), because "عِنْدَنا" is not a noun; but if you said "إنَّ الذِي عِنْدَنا" you would say "زَيْدٌ" ("the one who is with us is Zayd"), because "الذي عندَنا" is a noun. He said ﴿إِنَّمَا صَنَعُواْ كَيْدَ سَاحِرٍ﴾, making "إنَّ" and "ما" a single particle and letting "صَنَعُوا" govern, just as you say "إنَّما ضَرَبُوا زَيْداً" ("they only struck Zayd"). Whoever makes "ما" equivalent to "الذي" puts "الكيد" in the nominative.

akhfash:34-34.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿ذُرِّيَّةً بَعْضُهَا مِن بَعْضٍ﴾. He put it in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may also be a badal (substitute), [following] His saying ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ آدَمَ﴾. [And He the Exalted said]: ﴿إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ عِمْرَانَ رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّراً﴾; His saying ﴿مُحَرَّراً﴾ is a ḥāl.

akhfash:37-37.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنبَتَهَا نَبَاتاً حَسَناً وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا﴾. Some read ﴿وَكَفَلَها زكرياءُ﴾, and also ﴿كَفِلَها﴾ ﴿زَكَريّا﴾, and that is how we read; they are two dialect forms. Some read ﴿وَكَفِلَها زَكَرياء﴾ with kasra on the fāʾ. Whoever says "كَفَلَ" says "يَكْفُلُ", and whoever says "كَفِلَ" [says] "يَكْفَلُ". As for "كَفُلَ", I have not heard it, though it has been mentioned.
And He the Exalted said: ﴿يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾. This is like the Arabs' saying "يأكُلُ بِغَيْرِ حسابٍ" ("he eats without reckoning"), that is: no one is hard on him or restricts him. And ﴿سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ﴾ and ﴿أَسْرَعُ ٱلْحَاسِبِينَ﴾: He is saying "there is no pondering, deliberation or recollecting in His reckoning".

akhfash:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَّدُنْكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً﴾, because the nūn [in "لَدُنْ"] is quiescent, like the nūn of "مَنْ", and it is left in its quiescent state in the genitive construct, because it is not one of the nouns on which a vowel falls; that is why He said ﴿مِنْ لَدُنّا﴾, and He the Exalted said ﴿مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾, where it was left quiescent.
And He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ﴾, like "كثيرُ الدُّعاء" ("much in supplication"), because the alif and lām are permissible in it: you say "أنتَ السَّمِيعُ الدُّعاءِ". Its meaning is "you are one whose supplication is heard" [Translator's note: so in the text, «إِنَّكَ مَسْمُوعُ الدُّعاءِ»], that is: "You hear what is supplicated with".

akhfash:39-39.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿فَنَادَتْهُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ [وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي ٱلْمِحْرَابِ*] أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ﴾ [Translator's note: the explanation that follows concerns the reading إِنَّ with kasra], because it is as though He had said ﴿نَادَتْهُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ﴾ and they said ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ﴾, and what comes after "saying" is reported speech (ḥikāya). Some read ﴿أَنَّ اللّهَ﴾, saying: "the angels called to him with that".
And He the Exalted said: ﴿بِيَحْيَـىٰ مُصَدِّقاً بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَسَيِّداً وَحَصُوراً﴾. His saying ﴿وَسَيِّداً وَحَصُوراً﴾ is conjoined to "مُصَدِّقاً", as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

akhfash:40-40.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِي ٱلْكِبَرُ﴾, just as you say "وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِي الجَهْدُ" ("hardship has reached me"), that is: I am in hardship and old age.

akhfash:41-41.t: He said: ﴿ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلاَّ رَمْزاً﴾, meaning: "that you will not speak to people except by gesture"; He made it an exception falling outside the first part of the statement. Al-ramz is gesturing.

akhfash:42-42.t: He said: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ يٰمَرْيَمُ﴾: "إذْ" here has no khabar (complement) in the wording.

akhfash:44-44.t: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إِذْ يُلْقُون أَقْلاَمَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ﴾, because after everything that is a seeking of knowledge an interrogative may occur. You say "أَزَيْدٌ في الدّارِ؟" ("Is Zayd in the house?") and "لَتَعْلَمَنَّ أَزَيْدٌ فِي الدّار" ("you will surely know whether Zayd is in the house"). He said ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ﴾, that is: that We may see. And He the Exalted said ﴿لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلاً﴾. As for His saying ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَنزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عِتِيّاً﴾, it is not nominative for the same reason as the first, because His saying ﴿لَنَنزِعَنَّ﴾ is not a seeking of knowledge. But since "مَنْ" and "الذي" are [used] in places other than that of "أيّ", it became not fully declinable when it parted from its sisters, and it was left in one form, namely the ḍamma, and that is not inflection (iʿrāb). He made ﴿أَشَدّ﴾ part of its ṣila (relative clause). Some people have put it in the accusative, and that is analogically correct. They said: "When it is spoken, there is nothing in it but government [by the verb]." It has been read ﴿تَمَاماً عَلَى ٱلَّذِيۤ أَحْسَنُ﴾, with the nominative, making it part of the ṣila of "الذي"; and giving it fatḥa as a verb is better. They claimed that one of the Arabs said "ما أَنَا بالّذِي قائلٌ لكَ شَيْئاً" ("I am not the one who is saying anything to you"); this construction can only be, for the dual, "ما نَحْنُ بالَّلذَيْنِ قائِلانِ لَكَ شَيْئاً".

akhfash:7-7.t:
He said: ﴿هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾, and did not say "أُمَهاتُ" (mothers), just as you say to a man "I have no helper" and he says "We are your helper" ("نَحْنُ نَصِيرُكَ"). It resembles "دَعْنِي من تمْرَتان" ("leave me alone with 'two dates'"). [The poet] said [in the rajaz metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-second shāhid (attested verse)]:
تَعَرَّضْتِ لي بِمَكانٍ حِلِّ * تَعَرُّضَ المُهْرَةِ في الطِوَلِّ
* تَعْرُّضاً لَمْ تَأْلُ عَنْ قَتْلا لِي *
(You came across my path in an open place, as a filly sidles on her long tether — a sidling in which you spared no effort to kill me.)
He put it as reported speech (ḥikāya), because it was accusative before that, as you see; just as you say "نُودِيَ: الصلاةَ الصلاةَ" ("the call was made: 'The prayer! The prayer!'"), that is: you report his saying "الصلاةَ الصلاةَ". Some said: it is really "أَنْ قَتْلاً لِي", but he made it ʿayn, because in his dialect "أَنْ" is [pronounced] "عَنْ". The accusative is as a command, as though you said: "ضَرْباً لزَيْدٍ" ("a beating for Zayd!").
And He said: ﴿كُلٌّ مِّنْ عِندِ رَبِّنَا﴾, because something may be implied in "كُلّ", as He said ﴿إِنَّا كُلٌّ فِيهَآ﴾, meaning: all of us are in it. "كلّ" cannot have something implied in it when it is an adjective; it has something implied in it only when you make it a noun. [So] had it been "إِنَّا كُلاَّ فِيها" as an adjective, it would not be permissible, because implying [the pronoun] in it is weak and is not established everywhere.
And He said: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾. He is saying: "like their habit in evil", from "دَأَبَ", "يَدْأَبُ", "دَأَباً" (to persist in a habit).
And He said: ﴿قُلْ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَتُغْلَبُونَ وَتُحْشَرُونَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ﴾, that is: [say] "you will be overcome". Just as you say "Say to Zayd: 'You will go'", that is: [tell him] that you will go. Some read ﴿سَيُغْلَبُون﴾, that is: say to them what I say; and what I say [about] them is "they will be overcome". And He said ﴿قُل لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ إِن يَنتَهُواْ يُغَفَرْ لَهُمْ مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ وَإِنْ يَعُودُواْ﴾; this can only be with yāʾ [i.e. third person] in the Qur'an, because He said ﴿يُغْفَرْ لَهُمْ﴾; had it been with tāʾ [second person] He would have said ﴿يُغْفَرْ لَكُم﴾. In ordinary speech it is permissible with tāʾ, and you make it "لَكُمْ", as I have explained to you.
And He said: ﴿قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ ٱلْتَقَتَا فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَأُخْرَىٰ كَافِرَةٌ﴾: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), as though He had said "one of them is a party fighting in the way of Allah". It has also been read in the genitive, according to the first part of the statement, as a badal (substitute), and that is permissible. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-third shāhid (attested verse)]:
وَكُنْتُ كَذِي رِجْلَيْنِ رِجْلٌ صَحِيحَةٌ * وَرِجْلٌ بِها رَيْبٌ مِنَ الحَدَثان
(I was like a man with two legs: a sound leg, and a leg struck by one of fate's mishaps.)
He used the nominative. Some put it in the genitive as a badal, and some use the nominative on [the meaning] "one of them is such, and the other is such". And he said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-fourth shāhid]:
[و] إنَّ لها جارَيْنِ لَنْ يَغْدرا بها * ربيبُ النَبِيِّ وابنُ خَيْرِ الخَلائِفِ
([And] she has two protectors who will never betray her: the Prophet's stepson and the son of the best of caliphs.)
Nominative; and the accusative [would be] as a badal. And He the Exalted said ﴿هَـٰذَا [ذِكْرٌ] وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾ ﴿جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾: if you wish you may make "جنات" a badal as well; and if you wish you may put it in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ", or on [the meaning] "they are gardens", beginning with it. This cannot be on [the pattern] "one of them is such", because that meaning is not in it; and no one read it in the nominative. And He the Exalted said ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ﴾, accusative as a badal; the nominative may also occur in it, on [the meaning] "they are the jinn". And He the Exalted said ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نِبِيٍّ عَدُوّاً شَيَاطِينَ ٱلإِنْسِ﴾, as a badal, and nominative on [the meaning] "they are devils"; as though, when he uses the nominative, he were asked — or knew that he would be asked — "What are they?" or "Who are they?", and he said: "They are such-and-such". And when he uses the accusative, it is as though he were asked — or knew he would be asked — "He made what?" or "They made what?". Or it may be that the verb falls on "the devils", [and] ﴿عَدُوّاً﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Like it is ﴿لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ﴾ ﴿نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ﴾, as though that were asked or known, and he said "by a forelock"; the nominative may also occur in it, on [the question] "What is it?", so he says ﴿نَاصِيَةٌ﴾, and the accusative as a ḥāl. The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-fifth shāhid]:
إنّا وَجَدْنا بَنِي جُلاَّنَ كُلَّهُمُ * كَسَاعِدِ الضَّبِّ لا طُولٌ وَلا عِظَمُ
(We have found the Banū Jullān, all of them, like the foreleg of a lizard: no length and no bulk.)
As a badal, that is: like "no length and no bulk". And like the [nominative as] mubtadaʾ is ﴿قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ﴾.
And His saying ﴿قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ مِّن ذٰلِكُمْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَأَزْوَاجٌ مُّطَهَّرَةٌ﴾: it is as though it were said to them "What do they have?" and "What is that?", and it was said: "It is such-and-such". As for ﴿بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكَ مَثُوبَةً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, it is only on [the pattern] "I shall inform you of something worse than that in reckoning" and "of something better than that in reckoning". His saying ﴿مَن لَّعَنَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from His saying ﴿بِشَرٍّ﴾, and nominative on [the meaning] "it is the one whom Allah has cursed".

akhfash:45-45.t:
His saying ﴿إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ يٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ﴾ and ﴿يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُّحْضَراً﴾ — the like of this with "إذْ", "الحِين" (the time) and "يَوْم" (the day) is plentiful. That is good only because of the meaning: the Qur'an was sent down as command and [address], as though He said to them "Remember such-and-such" — and this occurs in the Qur'an in more than one place — and "Fear the day of such-and-such" or "the time of such-and-such".
And He the Exalted said: ﴿ٱسْمُهُ ٱلْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ وَجِيهاً﴾: He put it in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ is conjoined to ﴿وَجِيهاً﴾, and likewise ﴿وَكَهْلاً﴾ is conjoined to ﴿وَجِيهاً﴾, because that is accusative. As for His saying ﴿بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنْهُ ٱسْمُهُ ٱلْمَسِيحُ﴾, He made "the word" to be "ʿĪsā", because in meaning it is so; just as He said ﴿أَن تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يٰحَسْرَتَا﴾ and then said ﴿بَلَىٰ قَدْ جَآءَتْكَ آيَاتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِهَا﴾ [addressing the soul in the masculine], and just as they said "ذو الثُدَيَّة" ("the one with the little breast"), because his hand was like a breast: it was short and close to his breast, so he made it as though its name were "ثُدَيَّة"; were it not for that, the hāʾ would not have entered in the diminutive.

akhfash:47-47.t: As for His saying ﴿كَذَلِكِ ٱللَّهُ﴾, the kāf has kasra because it is addressing a woman; when the kāf is for a man it takes fatḥa. He said to the feminine ﴿وَٱسْتَغْفِرِي لِذَنْبِكِ إِنَّكِ كُنْتِ مِنَ ٱلْخَاطِئِينَ﴾.

akhfash:48-48.t: His saying ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُهُ ٱلْكِتَابَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative, [following] ﴿وَجِيهاً﴾. And ﴿رَسُولاً﴾ is conjoined to ﴿وَجِيهاً﴾.

akhfash:50-50.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمُصَدِّقاً لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ﴾, [following] His saying ﴿وَجِئْتُكُمْ﴾ ﴿مُصَدِّقاً لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيّ﴾ ﴿رَسُولاً﴾, because He said ﴿قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِآيَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾.

akhfash:51-51.t: He said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ﴾: ﴿إنَّ﴾ is a fresh start (ibtidāʾ). Some read ﴿أَنَّ﴾ with fatḥa, on [the meaning] "and I have come to you [with the sign] that Allah is my Lord and your Lord"; this is its meaning.

akhfash:52-52.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿فَلَمَّآ أَحَسَّ عِيسَىٰ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْكُفْرَ﴾, because this is from "أَحَسَّ", "يُحِسُّ", "إحْساساً" (to perceive), and not from His saying ﴿تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾, [since] that is from "حَسَّ", "يَحُسُّ", "حَسَّاً", which has a different meaning, because the meaning of "حَسَسْتُ" is "I killed", while "أَحْسَسْتُ" is "I supposed (ẓanantu)".

akhfash:59-59.t: [And He the Exalted said]: ﴿ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾: nominative as a fresh start (ibtidāʾ). Its meaning is: "Be", "and he was", as though He had said: "and there he is, existing".

akhfash:60-60.t: He said: ﴿ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾. He is saying: "It is the truth from your Lord."

akhfash:64-64.t:
He, Glorified and Exalted is He, said: ﴿يٰأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَابِ تَعَالَوْاْ إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍ سَوَآءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾. He put ﴿سَوَآءٍ﴾ in the genitive because it is an adjective of "the word", and it means "just". He meant "مُسْتَوِيَةٍ" (equal, even); had He meant "استواءً" (equality), it would have been accusative.
If one wished to take it in the sense of equality and still use the genitive, that would be permissible, making it an adjective of the word, like "الخَلْق", because "الخَلْق" can be an adjective and can be a noun. Allah the Exalted said ﴿ٱلَّذِي جَعَلْنَاهُ لِلنَّاسِ سَوَآءً ٱلْعَاكِفُ فِيهِ وَٱلْبَادِ﴾, because "السَّواء" belongs to the latter, and it is a noun, not an adjective, made to follow the former; that is when one means "equality" by it. If one means "مُسْتوِياً" (equal), it is permissible to make it follow the former; and the nominative in this sense is good, because it is an adjective that does not change from its state: it is not made dual, nor plural in its own form, nor feminine, and so it resembles nouns. And He the Exalted said ﴿أَن نَّجْعَلَهُمْ كَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ سَوَآءً مَّحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ﴾: "السواءُ" belongs to the living and the dying; this is the mubtadaʾ (subject). If you wish, you may make it follow the former, making it a preposed adjective connected with the former, so that it follows it; that is when you take it in the meaning of "equal", and [then] the nominative is the proper way of speech, as I have explained to you. As for His saying ﴿أَلاَّ نَعْبُدَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾, it is a badal (substitute), as though He had said "Come to [the word] that we worship none but Allah".

akhfash:72-72.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿آمِنُواْ بِٱلَّذِيۤ أُنْزِلَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَجْهَ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَٱكْفُرُوۤاْ آخِرَهُ﴾: He made it an adverbial (ẓarf).

akhfash:73-73.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿أَن يُؤْتَىۤ أَحَدٌ مِّثْلَ مَآ أُوتِيتُمْ﴾. He is saying: "Do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given, or that they will argue with you by it before your Lord", that is: and do not believe that they will argue with you.

akhfash:75-75.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَآئِماً﴾, because it is from "دُمْتُ", "تَدُومُ". A dialect of the Arabs has "دِمْتَ", and it is a reading, like "مِتَّ", "تَمُوتُ": he put it on "فَعِلَ", "يَفْعُلُ", and this is rare.
And He the Exalted said: ﴿بِدِينَارٍ﴾, that is: with a dinar [entrusted], as you say "مررتُ بِهِ" and "عليه" ("I passed by him / over him").

akhfash:77-77.t: He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلاَ يُكَلِّمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلاَ يَنظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾. This is like your saying to a man "ما تَنْظُرُ إِلَيَّ" ("you do not look at me") when he does not grant you anything.

akhfash:78-78.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ بِٱلْكِتَابِ ﴾, with fatḥa on the yāʾ. [Some] read ﴿يُلَوّوُنَ﴾ with ḍamma on the yāʾ. I consider it ﴿يَلْووُنَ﴾, because He said ﴿لَيّاً بألسنتهم﴾; had it been from ﴿يُلَووُّنَ﴾ it would have been "تَلْوِيَةً بألسنتهم".

akhfash:79-79.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ﴾: accusative, [following] ﴿مَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُؤْتِيهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ … ﴿ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ﴾, because "ثُمَّ" is one of the conjunctions.

akhfash:80-80.t: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْمُرَكُمْ﴾ is likewise conjoined in the accusative to ﴿أَنْ﴾. If you wish you may use the nominative, saying ﴿وَلاَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ﴾, not conjoining it to the first, meaning: and he does not command you.

akhfash:81-81.t: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿لَمَآ آتَيْتُكُم مِّن كِتَابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مُّصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾. The lām that is with "ما" at the beginning of the statement is the lām of ibtidāʾ (inception), as in "لزَيدٌ أَفضَلُ مِنكَ" ("Zayd is surely better than you"), because ﴿مَآ آتَيْتُكُمُ﴾ is a noun and what follows it is a ṣila (relative clause). The lām in ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُ﴾ is the lām of the oath, as though He had said "By Allah, you shall surely believe in him"; so He gave emphasis at the beginning of the statement and at its end, just as you say "أَمَا واللّهِ أَنْ لَوْ جِئْتَني لَكان كذا وكذا" ("By Allah, had you come to me, such-and-such would have happened"), though it can be dispensed with. He gave emphasis in ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ﴾ with the lām at the end of the statement, though it can be dispensed with. He made the khabar (predicate) of ﴿مَآ آتَيْتُكُمْ مِّن كِتَابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ﴾ to be ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾, like "What of ʿAbd Allāh? By Allah, you shall surely come to him." If you wish, you may make the khabar of (ما) ﴿مِنْ كِتابٍ﴾, meaning ﴿لَما آتَيْتُكُمْ كتابٌ وحِكْمَةٌ﴾ ("what I have given you is a Book and wisdom"), with "مِنْ" being redundant (zāʾida).

akhfash:91-91.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿مِّلْءُ ٱلأَرْضِ ذَهَباً﴾, with hamza, from "مَلأْتُ" ("I filled"). (ذَهَبا) is accusative just as you say "لِي مثلُكَ رَجُلاً" ("I have the like of you as a man"), that is: I have the like of you among men. That is because you occupied the genitive construct with the noun before "gold", namely "the earth"; then "gold" came, which is other than it, so it became accusative, just as the object becomes accusative when it comes after the agent. This is likewise the explanation of the ḥāl (circumstantial): when you say "جاء عبدُ الله راكباً" ("ʿAbd Allāh came riding"), you have occupied the verb with "ʿAbd Allāh", and "راكب" is not his adjective, because this is indefinite and that is definite; you brought it only to make it a noun for the state in which he came. That is how it is explained, and [likewise] the explanation of "هذا أحسنُ منكَ وَجْهاً" ("this one is better than you in face"): "the face" is other than the kāf on which "مِنْ" fell, and "أحسنُ" in the wording is only the one you are preferring; so "the face" is other than those two in the wording, and since it came after them and is other than them, it became accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) becomes accusative after the fāʿil (agent).

akhfash:93-93.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿كُلُّ ٱلطَّعَامِ كَانَ حِـلاًّ لِّبَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيل﴾, because one says "هذا حَلالٌ" and "هذا حِلٌّ" ("this is lawful"), and "هذا حَرام" and "هذا حِرْمٌ" ("this is forbidden"). It is read ﴿وَحَرَامٌ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ [and it is read] ﴿وحِرْمٌ على قرية﴾, and you say "حِرْمٌ عَليّكُم ذاك" ("that is forbidden to you"). Had one read ﴿وحُرْمٌ على قريةٍ﴾ it would have been permissible; [and had one read] ﴿وحَرْمٌ على قريةٍ﴾ it would also have been permissible.

akhfash:95-95.t: Allah said: ﴿فَٱتَّبِعُواْ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفاً﴾: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

akhfash:96-96.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ﴾: this is the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ".
Then He said ﴿مُبارَكاً﴾, because the khabar was already complete without it, so ﴿مُبارَكاً﴾ became accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهُدىً لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to it. The ḥāl is frequent in the Qur'an, and it occurs only where [the sentence] is already complete.

akhfash:97-97.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّـنَاتٌ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾. ﴿مَّقَامُ إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ is nominative because He is saying: ﴿فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ﴾, among them ﴿مَّقَامُ إِبْراهِيمَ﴾, by implication (iḍmār).

akhfash:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ كُنْتُمْ أَعْدَآءً﴾, by way of explanation, breaking off the statement at His saying ﴿ٱذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾; then He explained the sign of joining their hearts together and told of the state they were in before that joining, just as you say "أسمك الحائِطَ أَنْ يَميل" ("prop up the wall, lest it lean").
﴿وَكُنْتُمْ عَلَىٰ شَفَا حُفْرَةٍ﴾: "الشَّفا" (the brink) is maqṣūr (ending in a short alif) [Translator's note: the text has «متصور», evidently a misprint for «مقصور»], like "القَفا" (the nape), and its dual is with wāw: you say "شَفَوانِ", because imāla (inclining the alif towards yāʾ) does not occur in it; since imāla does not occur in it, you know that it is from wāw.

akhfash:104-104.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلْتَكُن مِّنْكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى ٱلْخَيْرِ﴾. "أُمَّةٌ" is singular in form and plural in meaning, which is why He said ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾. [In] ﴿وَلْتَكُنْ﴾ some also made the lām quiescent (jussive). [Translator's note: the text reads «جزم السلام», evidently for «جزم اللام», "made the lām quiescent".]

akhfash:106-106.t: As for His saying ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْوَدَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ أَكْفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ﴾, it is on [the meaning] "then it will be said to them: Did you disbelieve?", like His saying ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ﴾; this is plentiful in the Qur'an.

akhfash:109-109.t:
He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَللَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَإِلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ ٱلأُمُورُ﴾. He repeated the noun and made it overt; this is like "أمَّا زَيْدٌ فقد ذَهَبَ زَيْدٌ" ("as for Zayd, Zayd has gone"). The poet said [in the khafīf metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-seventh shāhid (attested verse)]:
لا أرَى المَوْتَ يَسْبِقُ الموتَ شَيءٌ * نَغَّصَ المَوْتُ ذا الغِنى والفَقِيرا
(I see nothing outrunning death; death has spoiled [life] for the rich and the poor.)
So he made [the noun] overt where a pronoun would be expected.

akhfash:110-110.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ﴾, meaning "people of a community (umma)", because al-umma is the way [of life]. And al-imma is also a dialect form. Al-Nābigha said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-ninth shāhid]:
حَلفْتُ فَلَمْ أَتْرُكْ لِنَفْسِكَ رِيبَةً * وَهَلْ يَأْثَمَنْ ذُو أُمَّةٍ وَهُوَ طائِعُ
(I swore, and left no doubt in your mind; and would a man of religion sin [by swearing falsely] while obedient?)

akhfash:111-111.t: He said: ﴿لَن يَضُرُّوكُمْ إِلاَّ أَذًى﴾: an exception falling outside the first part of the statement. It is as Yūnus related from one of the Arabs, who said "ما أَشْتَكِي شيئاً إلاَّ خَيْراً" ("I complain of nothing but good"). Like it is ﴿لاَّ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْداً وَلاَ شَرَاباً إِلاَّ حَمِيماً وَغَسَّاقاً﴾.

akhfash:112-112.t: [He said]: ﴿ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ أَيْنَ مَا ثُقِفُوۤاْ إِلاَّ بِحَبْلٍ مِّنْ ٱللَّهِ﴾. This is like ﴿لَنْ يَضُرُّوكُمْ إِلاَّ أَذَى﴾: an exception falling outside the first part of the statement, with the meaning of "لكنّ" (but); and it is no harder than His saying ﴿لاَّ يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْواً إِلاَّ سَلاَماً﴾.

akhfash:113-113.t:
He said: ﴿لَيْسُواْ سَوَآءً مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾, because He had mentioned them, then explained it and said: ﴿مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ أُمَّةٌ قَآئِمَةٌ يَتْلُونَ آيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, and did not say "and a community contrary to this community", because He had mentioned all this before. And He the Exalted said ﴿مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾, and this indicated a community contrary to this one.
He the Exalted said: ﴿آنَآءَ ٱللَّيْلِ﴾. The singular of "الآناءِ" is "إنَى", maqṣūr (ending in a short alif) — note this; some said "إِنْي", as you see, and "إنْوٌ"; it means the hours of the night. The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the one hundred and fifty-eighth shāhid]:
السَّالِكُ الثَّغْرَ مَخْشِيّاً مَوارِدُهُ * فِي كُلِّ إنيٍ قَضاهُ اللَّيلُ يَنْتَعِلُ
(Who travels the frontier pass whose watering-places are feared, putting on his sandals in every hour the night completes.)
He said: and I heard it as "يَخْتَعِلُ".

akhfash:118-118.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿لاَ يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالاً﴾, because it is from "ألَوْتُ" and "ما آلُو" "أَلْواً" ("I spare no effort").
And He the Exalted said: ﴿وَدُّواْ مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾. He is saying ﴿لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ بِطَانَةً﴾ ﴿وَدُّواْ﴾, that is: they loved ﴿مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾. He made it an adjective of "البِطانةَ" (the intimates), and put ﴿مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾ in the place of "العَنَتِ" (distress) [i.e. as an interpreted maṣdar].

akhfash:120-120.t: He said: ﴿لاَ يَضِرْكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ﴾, because it is from "ضار", "يَضِير" — and "ضِرْتُه", light, "فَأَنَا أَضِيرُه" ("I harm him"). Some read ﴿لا يضُرُّكُمْ﴾, making it from "ضَرَّ", "يَضُرُّ", and he vowelled [the final letter] because of the quiescent letter before it, since the doubled letter is equivalent to two letters, the first of which is quiescent. Some read ﴿لا يَضُرْكم﴾, making it from "ضار", "يضُور", which is a dialect form.

akhfash:121-121.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ تُبَوِّىءُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, because it is from "بَوَّأت" ("I settled [someone] in a place"). "إذْ" here has its khabar (complement) only in the meaning, as I have explained to you.

akhfash:125-125.t: He said: ﴿بِخَمْسَةِ آلاۤفٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ مُسِوِّمِينَ﴾, because they marked the horses. Some read ﴿مُسَوَّمينَ﴾, [meaning] marked, because they themselves were marked; and that is how we read.

akhfash:128-128.t: ﴿أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ﴾ [follows] ﴿لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفاً﴾: He conjoined it to the lām.

akhfash:140-140.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿إِن يَمْسَسْكُمْ قَرْحٌ﴾. Some read ﴿قُرْحٌ﴾, like "الضَعْف" and "الضُعْف". You say from it "قَرِحَ", "يَقْرَح", "قَرْحا" ("to be wounded"), and "هو قَرِح" ("he is wounded"). Some of the Arabs say "قَرِيح", like "مَذِل" and "مَذِيل".

akhfash:143-143.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ وَأَنْتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ﴾, as tawkīd (emphasis), just as you say "قَدْ رأيتُه واللّهِ بِعّيْني" ("By Allah, I saw him with my own eye") and "رَأَيْتُهُ عِيانا" ("I saw him plainly").

akhfash:144-144.t: He the Exalted said — and He did not say [it with a second interrogative] — ﴿أَفإِنْ مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ ٱنْقَلَبْتُمْ﴾, so as to give the alif a hamza [Translator's note: the opening of this passage is garbled in the text; the sense is that He did not say «أَأَنْقَلَبْتُمْ» with an interrogative hamza], because it is the answer of the conditional (jawāb al-mujāzāt) on which ﴿إِنْ﴾ has fallen, and the interrogative particle has already fallen on ﴿إِنْ﴾, so its complement does not need the interrogative, since its complement is like the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject). Do you not see that you say "أَزَيْدٌ حَسَنٌ" ("Is Zayd handsome?") and do not say "أَزَيْدٌ أَحَسَنٌ"? [Translator's note: the text has «أأَزَيْدٌ حَسَنٌ» with a doubled hamza, evidently a misprint.] Allah the Exalted said ﴿أَفَإِنْ مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلْخَالِدُونَ﴾ and did not say "أهُمُ اْلْخالِدُنَ", because it is the answer of the conditional.

akhfash:145-145.t: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوتَ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ الله كِتَاباً مُّؤَجَّلاً﴾. His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿كِتَاباً مُّؤَجَّلاً﴾ is tawkīd (emphasis), and it is accusative on [the meaning] "Allah has decreed that, a decree with a fixed term". Likewise everything in the Qur'an of His saying ﴿حَقّا﴾ is really "I make that a duty, as a duty" [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)]. Likewise ﴿وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, ﴿رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾, ﴿صُنْعَٱللَّهِ﴾ and ﴿كِتَابَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: it is really from "Allah made that, a making". This is the explanation of everything in the Qur'an of this kind, and it is plentiful.

akhfash:146-146.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن نَّبِيٍّ قُتِلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ فَمَا وَهَنُواْ﴾. He makes the Prophet the one who was killed, and that is the better of the two ways, because He had said ﴿أَفَإِنْ مَاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ﴾. Some read ﴿قَاتَلَ مَعَهُ﴾, and that is more common, and it is how we read, because they used to make ﴿قُتِلَ﴾ refer to ﴿رِبِّيُّون﴾. And we say: "So how do we say — so how do we say ﴿فَمَا وَهَنُواْ﴾ when we have said that they were killed?" It is, as I mentioned to you, that the killing refers to the Prophet ﷺ. His saying ﴿رِبِّيُّونَ﴾ means: those who worship the Lord the Exalted; its singular is "رِبِّيّ".

akhfash:147-147.t:
He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ﴾, and He said ﴿وَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُوۤاْ﴾, and [He said] ﴿مَّا كَانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ﴾. ﴿أَنْ قَالُواْ﴾ is the noun made nominative by ﴿وَكَانَ﴾, because the light ﴿أَنْ﴾ together with what it governs is equivalent to a noun; you say "أعْجَبَنِي أَنْ قالوا" ("their saying pleased me"). If you wish, you may put the first of all this in the nominative and make the last in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of kāna. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the one hundred and sixtieth shāhid]:
لَقَدْ عَلِمَ الأَقْوامُ ما كانَ دَاءَها * بِثَهْلانَ إلاَّ الخِزْيُ مِمَّنْ يَقُودُها
(The tribes have come to know that her malady at Thahlān was nothing but the disgrace of those who led her.)
And if you wish: "ما كانَ داؤُها الا الخِزْيَ".
